_note: GTEA, the 4 standard leave-one-subject-out splits (run each with --split 1..4; scripts/gtea_4fold.py runs all four and averages). The method of the paper, as on EgoPER: k-means centroids, cosine matching over HOD-masked frames. 4-split mean at beam_width 10: Acc 82.66, Edit 89.33, F1@{.1,.25,.5} 87.56 / 85.08 / 74.03; per split Acc 89.51 / 70.90 / 85.92 / 84.29.

features.name: feats_dinov2_hod_enclosed_15fps
features._backbone: DINOv2 ViT-L/14, patch tokens averaged inside the hand-object interaction box (Manipulation-Anchored Features), at the native 15 fps

boundary._note: 1.0 s x 15 fps = a 15-frame kernel. The paper text says L = 10 frames; 15 is what produced the paper's GTEA numbers, and 10 drops the 4-split Acc to 66.5. peak_height and min_distance are the GTEA values of the paper code.

prototypes._note: k = 3 centroids per action (the paper's GTEA setting; each recipe has 3 training videos per split). Micro-prototype windows are 1.5 s / 0.5 s stride as in the paper; a centroid is a single vector, so each yields one micro-prototype. seed is the k-means seed.

decoding._note: beam_width 10, as on EgoPER (the paper lists 5 for GTEA, which gives a 4-split Acc of 80.20). The five penalty terms are 0.0, as in every published run. bg_suppress_trigger is the literal string 'None' the paper's GTEA run passed: it names no GTEA action, so the rule never fires. The EgoPER microwave bridge is off.
